title: The Big Match
summary: Timur is the smallest player on his football team. In the final match of the season, his father finally comes to watch.
paragraphs: Timur was twelve years old, and football was the most important thing in his life. He played for his school team every Saturday, and he practised every day after school in the yard behind his building. He was the smallest player on the team, but he was fast, and he could pass the ball better than anyone.

There was only one problem. His father had never seen him play. He worked long hours as a taxi driver, often at weekends, and he was always too tired or too busy. Every Saturday, Timur looked at the people watching from the side of the field, hoping to see his father's face. He never did.

This season, Timur's team had done better than ever before. They had won eight games in a row, and now they were in the final against the best team in the city. On the Friday before the match, Timur asked his father again. “Please come tomorrow. It's the final.”
His father looked at him for a long time. “I have to work,” he said. “But I will try.”

On Saturday, the weather was cold and grey. Hundreds of people had come to watch, more than ever before. Timur searched the crowd, but his father was not there. He felt disappointed, but there was no time to think about it. The match was starting.

The other team was bigger and stronger. After twenty minutes, they scored the first goal. Timur's team fought hard, but at half time they were still losing one to nil. In the changing room, the coach told them not to give up. “Play together,” she said. “Pass the ball. Trust each other.”

In the second half, Timur played the best football of his life. He ran everywhere. Ten minutes before the end, he passed the ball perfectly to his friend Bobur, who scored. It was one each. The crowd went wild.

Then, in the last minute of the match, Timur got the ball near the middle of the field. He saw a space and started running. One defender tried to stop him, then another. He was close to the goal now. He kicked the ball as hard as he could. It flew past the goalkeeper's hands and into the net.
For a moment, Timur could not hear anything. Then his teammates were jumping on him, and everyone was shouting. The referee blew the whistle. They had won.

As Timur walked off the field, he heard a voice calling his name. He turned around. Standing by the gate, still wearing his taxi driver's jacket, was his father. “I saw it,” his father said, his eyes full of tears. “I saw the whole second half. I told my boss I had something more important to do.” Timur ran to him, and his father held him tight. It was the best day of Timur's life, and it was not only because of the goal.

questions.question: What was Timur good at?
options: Passing the ball and running fast
questions.explanation: He was fast and could pass the ball better than anyone.

questions.question: Why had Timur's father never seen him play?
options: He worked long hours, often at weekends
Timur did not want him there
questions.explanation: He worked long hours as a taxi driver, often at weekends.

questions.question: What was the score at half time?
options: One to nil to Timur's team
One to nil to the other team
questions.explanation: At half time Timur's team were losing one to nil.

questions.question: How did Timur help his team score the first goal?
options: He passed the ball to Bobur
questions.explanation: He passed the ball perfectly to Bobur, who scored.

questions.question: Why was it the best day of Timur's life 'not only because of the goal'?
options: His father came to watch him
questions.explanation: His father finally came and saw him play.

grammar.structure: Past perfect for background (had done / had won)
grammar.explanation: Had + past participle gives background information about what happened before the main events of the story.
grammar.example: They had won eight games in a row, and now they were in the final against the best team in the city.

exercise.question: Choose the correct form: By the final, Timur ___ in every game of the season.
exercise.explanation: The games happened before the final, so we use had played.

grammar.structure: Reported commands (tell someone + not + to + verb)
grammar.explanation: To report an instruction, we use tell + person + (not) to + verb.
grammar.example: In the changing room, the coach told them not to give up.

exercise.question: The coach said: “Don't stop running!” Choose the reported sentence.
options: The coach told them don't stop running.
The coach told them not to stop running.
The coach told them to not stopping.
The coach said them not stop running.
exercise.explanation: Negative command: told + person + not to + verb.

grammar.structure: Word + preposition: look at, listen to
grammar.explanation: We look at something and listen to something. These prepositions always go with these verbs.
grammar.example: His father looked at him for a long time.

exercise.question: Choose the correct word: Please listen ___ the teacher.
exercise.explanation: listen to. In Uzbek “...ni tinglamoq” has no extra word, but English needs to.
